Bug_Title: "@Bean" methods for Singleton should not be invoked in "@Configuration" when proxyBeanMethods is false
Bug_Details:
When setting the proxyBeanMethods attribute to false the @Bean methods are not proxied and this is similar
to removing the @Configuration stereotype. In this scenario, @Bean methods within the @Configuration annotated
class operate in lite
mode , resulting in a new bean creation each time the method is invoked.
For Singleton beans, this could cause unexpected outcomes as the bean is created multiple times instead of being created once and
cached.
The rule raises an issue when the proxyBeanMethods attribute is set to false and the @Bean method of a Singleton bean is directly invoked in the @Configuration annotated class code.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by directly invoking the @Bean method mySingletonBean() within the showBug() method of the SingletonBeanBug class. Since proxyBeanMethods is false, this results in multiple instances of MySingletonBean being created instead of a single instance.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug() method of the SingletonBeanBug class. Inside the showBug() method, the mySingletonBean() method is called twice, creating two different instances of MySingletonBean due to proxyBeanMethods being false. The test then asserts that the hashcodes of the two beans are not equal, which will fail because they are indeed different instances.
